title: Nested records: orders with customer and items
description: Headers nest: customer is a record <…> inside the record, items a list of records <[…]>; nested values stay positional.
question: What is the total (qty × price) of every paid order?

toon.none:
The data below is in TOON.

TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) — how to read it:
- Indentation shows nesting; "key: value" is a field.
- key[N]{f1,f2,...}: is followed by N rows of comma-separated values in field order.
- key[N]: a,b,c is a list of N values; "- " starts an item of a list of objects.

<data>
orders[3]:
  - id: ORD-1001
    status: paid
    customer:
      id: 7
      name: Hedy Johnson
      country: PL
    items[2]{sku,qty,price}:
      KB-01,2,89
      MS-02,1,39.5
  - id: ORD-1002
    status: pending
    customer:
      id: 9
      name: Ada Torvalds
      country: DE
    items[1]{sku,qty,price}:
      HD-10,1,129.9
  - id: ORD-1003
    status: paid
    customer:
      id: 7
      name: Hedy Johnson
      country: PL
    items[2]{sku,qty,price}:
      DK-05,1,199
      KB-01,1,89
</data>

Question: What is the total (qty × price) of every paid order?

Answer in TOON only (no prose, no code fences): paid[N]{id,total}: followed by one row per item.

akd.none:
The data below is in AK-DATA.

AK-DATA (Arkadia Data Format): <a:type,b:type> is a header; (v1,v2) is a record whose values follow the header order.
<[a:type,...]>[(...),(...)] is a list of records sharing that header; headers nest, e.g. items:<[sku:string,qty:number]>.
{key:value} is a record with names; <type> or <any> before a value overrides the header type.
Strings are quoted; numbers, true, false, null as in JSON; /*...*/, $attr, #tag are metadata, not data.
A record with fewer values than its header has only the first fields; //$size=N// before list items is their count.

<data>
<orders:<[
  id:string,
  status:string,
  customer:<id:number, name:string, country:string>,
  items:<[sku:string, qty:number, price:number]>
]>>
([
  ("ORD-1001", "paid", (7, "Hedy Johnson", "PL"),
   [("KB-01", 2, 89.0), ("MS-02", 1, 39.5)]),
  ("ORD-1002", "pending", (9, "Ada Torvalds", "DE"), [("HD-10", 1, 129.9)]),
  ("ORD-1003", "paid", (7, "Hedy Johnson", "PL"),
   [("DK-05", 1, 199.0), ("KB-01", 1, 89.0)])
])
</data>

Question: What is the total (qty × price) of every paid order?

Answer in AK-DATA only (no prose, no code fences), with exactly this header and one record per item:
<paid:<[id:string,total:number]>>
